text.tspan: Incoming customer phone calls initiate interactions with the call center.
These calls are received and managed within the sales and customer service environment.
Within this environment, the interaction center orchestrates call workflows.
Audio recordings from calls and follow-up customer satisfaction surveys are captured.
The recorded interaction files and associated metadata are exported to central storage.
A centralized Hadoop repository aggregates interaction logs and supplies data to downstream processing clusters.
The development cluster handles model building and experimental validation.
Here, audio is transcribed to text, feature embeddings are generated,
and ranking models are trained and calibrated before deployment.
The production cluster executes the end-to-end analytical pipeline on live call streams.
The call satisfaction analysis module ingests call files directly from Hadoop for real-time scoring.
The pipeline converts speech to text, computes call embedding vectors,
and applies graph-based ranking with isotonic regression to predict satisfaction scores.
Predicted representative satisfaction scores and aggregated group metrics are archived in the database.
Finally, managers access monitoring dashboards to identify customer dissatisfaction and take timely operational actions.
